translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Monday of the festival of Shavuos,
the year 5746*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that at the Giving of the Torah there was a revelation of "You have been shown to know that Hashem is the Elokim, there is none else besides Him," as interpreted by the Alter Rebbe in Tanya, involving a sensory vision and the dew of Torah that revives the dead.

translations.translation: "You have been shown to know that Hashem is the Elokim, there is none else besides Him,"
is written in Mishneh Torah
(which Moshe said from his own mouth),
and our master the Alter Rebbe explains in Sefer HaTanya
that this matter was at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
for then there was the revelation of "You have been shown to know," etc.,
according to the teaching of the Alter Rebbe:
"You" — You, the Essence (Atzmus) of Ein Sof, blessed be He, "have been shown" — You have revealed Yourself, "to know" — that one should know You,
"that Hashem is the Elokim, there is none else besides Him,"
which are
two modes and matters of comprehension in the comprehensions of Divinity:
the first is the comprehension that Hashem and Elokim are entirely one, and the second is the comprehension of "there is none else besides Him."
And in the Tanya there, he explains,
that at the time of the Giving of the Torah there was this revelation
(of His Essence, etc.)
in a manner of "You have been shown"
(and he adds)
literally with sensory sight.
And the Tanya continues there,
that therefore
(Israel)
were in a state of actual self-nullification, as our sages said
(in the Gemara)
that at every single utterance their souls flew away, etc., and the Holy One, blessed be He, restored them with the dew with which He will revive the dead,
and as it is stated in the Gemara there that this is what King Dovid said
(whose yahrtzeit is on Shavuos)
"A generous rain You will pour down, O Elokim; Your inheritance, when it was weary, You established it,"
which refers to the dew of revival with which He revived Israel,
and the Tanya explains there,
that this dew is the dew of Torah, etc., as our sages said,
"Whoever engages in Torah, the dew of Torah revives him," etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of souls departing at each utterance and being revived by the dew of Torah serves as a lesson in divine service, and that at the time of the Giving of the Torah this revelation is drawn down into every aspect of a person's existence.

translations.translation: And behold, the explanation of our teacher the Baal Shem Tov is known
(whose yahrtzeit is on Shavuos),
that every matter in the world is a lesson in the service of man to his Creator.
And all the more so, a fortiori, every matter in the Torah,
as it is written,
"And Hashem commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Hashem our Elokim," etc.,
for from this verse it is proven
that the entire Torah
(all these statutes)
its purpose is a lesson in the service of Hashem,
"to fear Hashem our Elokim," etc.,
even down to the simple fulfillment of the commandments.
And from this it is understood
that also this matter in the Torah,
that at every single utterance their souls flew away and He restored them with the dew, etc.,
is a lesson in the service of man to his Creator.
And furthermore,
behold, our teacher the Baal Shem Tov explains in Kesser Shem Tov
on the statement of our sages,
"Know what is above from you,"
meaning: from yourself you shall know,
whatever attribute is aroused in you, so it is above
[and elsewhere
it is brought in the name of the Maggid,
and in a third place
it is brought in the name of the Alter Rebbe,
and there are variations in language between them,
and the place is not here].
And from this it is understood,
that when a person sees and knows in himself
(from yourself)
that for him it is the time of the Giving of our Torah
(since it is so explicitly stated in the Torah of Truth and the Torah of Life),
then it is understood from this,
that so it is also above,
that above it is the time of the Giving of our Torah.
That is to say,
that at the time of the Giving of our Torah, "You have been shown to know that Hashem is the Elokim, there is none else besides Him" was actualized,
You, the Essence of Ein Sof, blessed be He, revealed Yourself, etc.,
"You have been shown" literally with sensory sight,
and together with this, there was also drawn into Israel the dew with which He will revive the dead, which is the dew of Torah.
And this matter is drawn into all aspects of a person,
(in the manner of what is written,
"This is the Torah, man"),
that the Torah
(also the aspect of the dew of Torah)
penetrates the existence of a person until it becomes the true existence of each and every one of Israel,
including in all your ways and in all your deeds
(as explained elsewhere
the matter of this).
And from this it is understood even more,
that this matter
(the dew of Torah)
pertains to the service of man in the present time.
